NCBIGene:672, name: BRCA1 DNA repair associated [1], is linked to the diseases Familial cancer of breast [2], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 1 [3], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 4 [4], and Fanconi anemia complementation group S [5]. NCBIGene:675, name: BRCA2 DNA repair associated [6], is linked to the diseases Medulloblastoma [7], Fanconi anemia complementation group D1 [8], Familial breast-ovarian cancer susceptibility 2 [9], Glioma susceptibility 3 [10], Familial prostate cancer [11], Pancreatic cancer susceptibility 2 [12], and Wilms tumor 1 [13].

Gene NCBIGene:672, name: BRCA1 DNA repair associated [1]. Gene NCBIGene:675, name: BRCA2 DNA repair associated [6]. gene symbol: BRCA1 [14]. gene name: BRCA1 [17]. This gene encodes a 190 kD nuclear phosphoprotein that plays a role in maintaining genomic stability, and it also acts as a tumor suppressor [23]. The BRCA1 gene contains 22 exons spanning about 110 kb of DNA [23]. The encoded protein combines with other tumor suppressors, DNA damage sensors, and signal transducers to form a large multi-subunit protein complex known as the BRCA1-associated genome surveillance complex (BASC) [23]. This gene product associates with RNA polymerase II, and through the C-terminal d [23].

Approximately 1-5% of breast cancers are attributed to inherited mutations in BRCA1 or BRCA2 and are selectively sensitive to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors [42]. In other cancer types, germline and/or somatic mutations in BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 (BRCA1/BRCA2) also confer selective sensitivity to PARP inhibitors [42]. Thus, assays to detect BRCA1/BRCA2-deficient tumors have been sought [42]. Recently, somatic substitution, insertion/deletion and rearrangement patterns, or 'mutational signatures', wer [42]. The breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility gene (BRCA1) is a tumor suppressor whose mutation has been associated with the development of breast, ovarian and, probably, other malignancies at young ages [44]. The BRCA1 gene product participates in multiple biological pathways including the DNA damage response, transcriptional control, cell growth and apoptosis [44]. Inactivating germline mutations of the BRCA1 gene can be detected in a substantial portion of families with inherited breast and/or ovarian c [44]. Women with germline BRCA1 mutations (BRCA1+/mut) have increased risk for hereditary breast cancer [46]. Cancer initiation in BRCA1+/mut is associated with premalignant changes in breast epithelium [46]. however, the role of the epithelium-associated stromal niche during BRCA1-driven tumor initiation remains unclear [46]. Here we show that the premalignant stromal niche promotes epithelial proliferation and mutant BRCA1-driven tumorigenesis in trans [46]. Using single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of human preneoplas [46]. DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair by homologous recombination is initiated by DNA end resection, a process involving the controlled degradation of the 5'-terminated strands at DSB sites1,2 [48]. The breast cancer suppressor BRCA1-BARD1 not only promotes resection and homologous recombination, but it also protects DNA upon replication stress1,3-9 [48]. BRCA1-BARD1 counteracts the anti-resection and pro-non-homologous end-joining factor 53BP1, but whether it functions in resection directly has been uncle [48]. BRCA1 is one of the most frequently-mutated tumor suppressor genes in ovarian and breast cancers [50]. Loss of BRCA1 triggers homologous recombination (HR) repair deficiency, consequently leading to genomic instability and PARP inhibitors (PARPi)-associated synthetic lethality [50]. Although, the roles of BRCA1 in DNA repair and replication have been extensively investigated, its tumor suppressive functions beyond genome safeguard remain poorly understood [50].
